title: Object
spec: Start by setting up a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero degrees for all axes and a translation vector also set to zero. Next, create a new face and draw the first loop consisting of four lines to form a rectangle. The first line starts at the origin (0.0, 0.0) and ends at (0.75, 0.0). The second line runs from (0.75, 0.0) to (0.75, 0.0375). The third line goes from (0.75, 0.0375) to (0.0, 0.0375), and the fourth line completes the rectangle by connecting (0.0, 0.0375) back to the origin. After drawing the rectangle, apply a scaling factor of 0.75 to the entire sketch to adjust its size. Transform the scaled 2D sketch into 3D space by rotating it using the same Euler angles and translating it with the same vector as initially set. Finally, extrude the sketch along the normal direction by 0.1275 units to create a 3D rectangular prism. Ensure that the extrusion does not occur in the opposite direction. Integrate this new solid body with any previous bodies to form the complete model. The resulting object is a rectangular prism with a cylindrical base, featuring a flat rectangular top surface and a circular bottom surface. The dimensions are as follows: length of 0.75 units, width of 0.0375 units, and height of 0.1275 units.

reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create the sketch for the rectangular base
r = r.box(0.75, 0.0375, 0.1275, centered=(False, False, False))

lanes.label: Cadabra 4B (ours) · best of 8
lanes.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.75, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0375) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a rectangular prism
r = r.extrude(0.1275)
